## Found during #536 browser qualification

The actual VM phone-control HTTP/uinput/browser path passes pointer hover/down/up/click, button activation, typing/deletion, wheel scrolling, the intended authentication host and Close. Backspace on the noneditable next page does not go back despite the window hint saying B back. The original actual-browser receipt records browser_back=false; no tablet user-agent change is justified.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: the owned credential-free local provider has two pages and a text field. Test Back on the second page, preserve Backspace editing in a field, and verify Close still exits. No owner device or real provider account is needed.

Already written: the existing browser has no explicit Back behavior outside its on-screen keyboard; WebKitGTK does not provide the expected navigation in this tested path. No credentials or cloud files were changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Actual local-provider navigation goes back on B/Backspace when no editable control owns the key; the original failure and corrected result are retained.
- [x] Text fields retain ordinary character deletion, provider-handled keys and modified shortcuts are not repurposed, and Close/popup return continue to work.
- [x] Source/binary binding, runtime events and reviewed flow frames update #536's canonical evidence before the next pin.

M7.P5 under #344, coupled to #536. The maintainer authorized completing all diagnosed fixes. This adds the missing behavior advertised by the existing hint, without changing its copy.

## Implemented and locally verified — 2026-10-11

Actual WebKit testing now passes all16 recorded controls, including Back outside editing, text deletion, provider-handled keys, modified keys, popup/opener return and Close. The original browser_back=false result is preserved. Its build/deployment binding is reconstructed explicitly from retained build and matching guest payload, without inventing a contemporaneous browser12 process receipt.

Proof: `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-network-cloud-management/browser/` and `browser-original/`. Source binary408480959f05132e7fb5cdf5013bb0f4ea4b98cfb178cb85f6dfb712519e1170; canonical input-flow evidence is updated in the feature worktree. No user-agent change, live personal login, pin promotion or firmware deployment. The scoped independent review and source integration remain open.

## Verified source delivery — 2026-10-11T16:27:55.227775+00:00

Distribution [bc2dceb406](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/commit/bc2dceb406969a401d987de168acfb3ae60b7e01) and ES [c8dc72cf9e](https://github.com/pixelelated/emulationstation/commit/c8dc72cf9ec00ab00d6c4a9fcdcea1746c6f1f78) are integrated and pushed. Final delivery head `849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f` has successful exact-head hosted record and private-word checks. [Canonical flow/evidence packet](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-network-cloud-management); [independent audit, all seven repairs and Phase7 resolution](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f/docs/audits/2026_10_11-epic-m7-network-cloud-344).

AC1–2: browser/result.json has all16 actual WebKit controls true, including navigation Back, field deletion, handled/modified keys, popup return and Close; browser-original retains the original failure. AC3: source/binary/event bindings and reviewed BR01 frames precede the published pin.

Only owned VM/local synthetic endpoints were used. The source fix is delivered; no new firmware image, owner-device update or personal-cloud action is claimed. Combined-image release qualification remains under #344/#537.
